draft.title: The rise of Islam
card: Islam began in Arabia in the 7th century CE. Its prophet was Muhammad, and his followers are called Muslims.
After Muhammad's death in 632 CE, Muslim rule spread quickly. Within about a hundred years it stretched from Spain in the west to Central Asia in the east.
Baghdad became a great centre of learning. Scholars there studied and translated older Greek, Persian and Indian works.
They did more than keep old knowledge. They also added new ideas in science, maths and medicine.
draft.remember: Islam grew from Arabia into a large empire, and its scholars both kept and added to knowledge.

a.q: What did scholars in Baghdad do with learning from earlier peoples?
opts: Kept it and added new ideas in science, maths and medicine
Kept it safe but made no new discoveries of their own
Replaced it with new ideas that came only from Arabia
Sent it to Europe, where all new discoveries were made
a.why: The scholars translated older Greek, Persian and Indian works and also added new ideas. The tempting option about only keeping knowledge is wrong because the scholars advanced learning as well.
a.clue: They did two things with knowledge, not just one.

b.q: Which statement about the early spread of Islam is correct?
opts: It began in Arabia and spread quickly after Muhammad's death
It began in Spain and spread slowly to Arabia
It began in Baghdad and stayed within Arabia
It began in Central Asia and spread to Arabia in 476 CE
b.why: Islam began in Arabia in the 7th century. After Muhammad died in 632 CE, Muslim rule spread quickly across a huge area. Baghdad was a centre of learning, not the place where Islam began.
b.clue: Think about where Islam began and how fast it grew.

a.best: Kept it and added new ideas in science, maths and medicine

b.best: It began in Arabia and spread quickly after Muhammad's death

check.summary: No problems found. The dates and places are accurate, both questions have one clearly right answer, and the explanations match the card.
